description: Correctness of value IN (uncorrelated subquery) after the membership test was changed from a per-outer-row linear scan to a hash index. The index must reproduce the engine's IN equality EXACTLY: scale-insensitive numeric equality across types, so an integer 4 matches a double 4.0; toString equality for strings; and NULLs that never match a non-NULL value. NOT IN carries three-valued logic - a set containing a NULL makes every miss UNKNOWN, so NOT IN is never TRUE and filters every row, while excluding the NULL member makes the misses definite. Converted 1:1 from query/InSubqueryMembershipTest (now retired); the Java counted rows only, so a filter that kept the WRONG row would have passed - each converted test names the rows it keeps.
